tasks.title: Normalize keybind mnemonics across zellij/nvim/inner tools
tasks.notes: Semantic consistency of the mnemonic letter, not just collision-avoidance: a given letter should mean the same verb everywhere (e.g. m=move in zellij, not 'mark' elsewhere). Goal: lower cognitive load. Follow-up from the zellij quick-terminal/mode-alignment branch. Collision checker exists (scripts/check-keybind-collisions.py); this is about meaning, not overlap. Also revisit nvim-vs-zellij/ghostty collisions (nvim maps only apply in-pane; zellij globals shadow them).

tasks.title: Install lazygit + wire into nvim and broot
tasks.notes: Researched 2026-07-23. Two consumers: (1) nvim plugin — value narrowed to interactive rebase, partial staging, history browse/cherry-pick; everything else covered by alt+f/delegation. (2) broot: conf.hjson already defines a Ctrl-g verb ('lazygit --path {directory}') that errors harmlessly until lazygit is installed. Shared prereq: add install_lazygit to CLI-extras (packaged on zypper; Ubuntu needs a release binary/PPA). LIGHT scope. Deferred for now. See references.

tasks.title: Document GUI/desktop tools wanted on every new machine
tasks.notes:
Gap between 'configs symlinked' and 'machine actually ready'. Start as docs/tools.md (tool, why, install command per package manager) rather than install.sh logic - package names differ across zypper/apt/pacman, flatpak-vs-native is a per-machine call, and install.sh assuming a package manager cuts against the minimal-dependencies principle. Promote into the installer later if the list stabilizes. Same shape as nvim-lazygit.

Scope now covers CLI tools too, not just GUI/desktop - suggest two sections in docs/tools.md, since the CLI half is natively packaged and scriptable and could plausibly be promoted into install.sh, while GUI stays a per-machine judgment call.

GUI entries: DBeaver (settled - go-to SQL GUI, flatpak io.dbeaver.DBeaverCommunity). S3/cloud storage GUI slot resolved as 'no GUI needed' - S3Drive evaluated and rejected (paywalled multi-file download, and unwilling to hand AWS creds to a freemium client); FileZilla Pro and Cyberduck/duck not pursued since aws-cli covers file moves and rclone covers the rest.

CLI entries (all installed and working as of 2026-07-28): aws-vault v7.2.0 for credentials - NOT packaged for openSUSE, install the binary from GitHub releases; uses AWS_VAULT_BACKEND=file (encrypted store at ~/.awsvault/keys) rather than the KWallet/Secret Service default, so the creds stay isolated from the desktop keyring. rclone for S3 - configure the remote with env_auth=true so it reads from aws-vault instead of storing its own copy, and 'rclone mount --vfs-cache-mode full' makes the bucket a normal directory that any tool (duckdb included) can read. duckdb for parquet - see duckdb-setup.

tasks.title: Split bootstrap into private repo depending on public dotfiles
tasks.notes: Two repos along a privacy line, dependency points one way only: PUBLIC dotfiles (configs, symlinks, install.sh - self-contained, useful to a stranger, never learns bootstrap exists) <- PRIVATE bootstrap (clones dotfiles, runs ./install.sh, then packages + private repos + per-repo setup). Why this works: keeps dotfiles genuinely publishable rather than publishable-with-holes, and confines the non-idempotent cloning/setup-script mess to the private repo so install.sh keeps its symlink-only idempotency. Precedent set: bootstrap orchestrates dotfiles via its existing clean ./install.sh entrypoint - suggests other repos (claude-toolkit, claude-sessions, schema-smith) should expose the same, rather than bootstrap knowing their internals. Publishability checked 2026-07-27: no work identifiers, hardcoded home paths, or credential-shaped strings in tracked files; .gitconfig NOT reviewed (secrets-guard hook) - check it for email/signing key/includeIf before publishing. OPEN: does new-machine-tools go public (generic GUI tools) or private (if it accumulates work-specific tooling)?

tasks.title: Sanitize tracked .gitconfig before making repo public
tasks.notes: Repo is private, so real identities in tracked files are acceptable today. If it ever goes public: tracked .gitconfig holds user.email (dsuazop@gmail.com) and includeIf paths naming the raiz/blumar work trees; docs/gitconfig-conditional-includes.md additionally names all three GitHub accounts and both work email domains. Cheapest fix: move [user] out of the tracked .gitconfig into an untracked ~/.gitconfig-local pulled in via [include], mirroring how ~/.gitconfig-raiz and ~/.gitconfig-blumar already work — tracked file becomes structure only, no template/substitution step, symlink keeps working. The includeIf directory names (raiz/blumar) remain structural and can only be removed by untracking. Note .gitconfig is symlinked to ~/.gitconfig, so it cannot hold placeholders while also being the live config.

tasks.title: Set up Bitwarden CLI for personal credentials
tasks.notes: Bitwarden is already the password manager in use on Windows and phone; this is about getting it usable from the Linux CLI. Open decision: official 'bw' (Node, npm install -g @bitwarden/cli or native binary from releases - check 'zypper se bitwarden', likely not in openSUSE repos) vs 'rbw' (unofficial Rust client, much faster, has an unlock agent so you are not re-entering the master password constantly; third-party client for the password vault, which is its own trust call). Official bw is required for anything touching org/admin operations. Session handling is the main friction: bw needs BW_SESSION exported and it expires - do NOT put it in .bashrc, it is a live vault-unlock token. Distinct from aws-vault, which stays as-is for AWS only.

tasks.title: Explore Bitwarden CLI for programmatic secret retrieval
tasks.notes: Direction, not a settled plan: use the Bitwarden CLI as a general secret-retrieval layer in scripts instead of scattering tokens across dotfiles and .env files. Shape is 'bw get password NAME' / 'bw get item NAME | jq' inline at the point of use. Depends on bitwarden-cli-setup landing first (client choice + session/agent handling). Two habits worth establishing up front: never persist BW_SESSION in shell init, and prefer passing secrets inline to the single command that needs them over 'export TOKEN=$(bw get ...)', which exposes them to every child process - same reasoning as 'aws-vault exec'. Bitwarden could also be the source of truth for the AWS key (it syncs to phone/Windows, ~/.awsvault/keys never will), seeding 'aws-vault add' - but Bitwarden should NOT be in the hot path for AWS, since that would trade away aws-vault's short-lived STS sessions for a long-lived key in the environment.

tasks.title: expected_dests hardcodes ghostty as GUI-only, duplicating GROUP_FLAGS gating
tasks.notes:
tests/helpers.sh's expected_dests has a case arm skipping the ghostty group, because a headless run never prompts for it. Since v0.1.20 the runtime gates the same thing via GROUP_FLAGS in links.sh. Two independent encodings of 'ghostty is special' that agree today.

Adding a second GUI-only group will need a matching case arm in helpers.sh and nothing will remind the author — the failure surfaces as a confusing link-set diff in test_install.sh rather than a clear message.

Deliberately deferred during feat/links-new-category-flow: fixing it means teaching the test harness about headless-ness, which is a larger change than that task. Not urgent — ghostty is the only GUI-only group today.

tasks.title: GROUP_FLAGS couples links.sh to install.sh flag names by string
tasks.notes:
Since v0.1.20, links.sh's GROUP_FLAGS names INSTALL_* variables that live in install.sh, resolved indirectly via ${!flag:-}. Renaming a flag in install.sh produces no error anywhere — the group just silently stops linking.

Mitigation in place: tests/test_links.sh asserts every GROUP_FLAGS flag matches a '^FLAG=false$' line in install.sh's initializer block. That works but is mildly brittle to reformatting of that block (e.g. switching to ': ${INSTALL_X:=false}' or one-lining the declarations would break the grep without any real defect).

Worth revisiting only if the initializer block gets reformatted or the assertion produces a false failure. The alternative is accepting the silent-failure class, or moving to a single declaration site — but flags are prompt state owned by install.sh and meaningless to uninstall.sh, which sources the same links.sh.
